key_insight: Algorithmic recourse is only reliable when it accounts for causal effects; otherwise, recommended changes can trigger strategic gaming, shift the data distribution, and undermine future model performance.
engineering_relevance: For deployed decision systems in credit and lending, causal recourse can improve fairness and stability by producing actionable recommendations that remain valid after user responses and model retraining.
method: Model recourse actions through a structural causal model to capture feature interactions and true-label effects.
Formulate the resulting recourse problem in a causal performative framework, yielding a non-convex optimization landscape.
Use simple iterative dynamics to search for performatively stable solutions.
evidence_signal: Experiments on semi-synthetic and real credit datasets show the proposed causal recourse approach outperforms standard empirical risk minimization while reducing the need for repeated retraining under strategic behavior.
watch_item: The approach depends on specifying a credible causal model; misspecified causal assumptions could weaken stability and the quality of recourse recommendations.
paper_title: The Role of Causality in Algorithmic Recourse
